source.title: Jailbreaking Leaves a Trace: Understanding and Detecting Jailbreak Attacks from Internal Representations of Large Language Models
source.citation: Sri Durga Sai Sowmya Kadali et al., 2026
source.authors: Sri Durga Sai Sowmya Kadali; E. Papalexakis

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some tables and figures are flattened in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes jailbreak-related representations and tests a layer-bypass defense, but does not find, add, or remove the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, nor test any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study uses CP-decomposed representations and per-layer classifiers to distinguish jailbreak from benign prompts, then bypasses layers selected by susceptibility scores. It does not measure a difference-in-means refusal direction or test whether that direction mediates refusal. Its results concern jailbreak detection and a different layer-bypass defense; they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses mlabonne's abliterated LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct as a testbed and states such models 'lack safety mechanisms'. That takes V2 as given rather than measuring it: no refusal rate or ASR is reported for the abliterated model without the bypass. Its results are its own CP-tensor jailbreak classifier and a layer-bypass defense. Neither finds, adds or ablates a difference-in-means refusal direction, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that internal representations carry consistent jailbreak signatures across model families, enabling detection. They also conclude that bypassing high-susceptibility layers disrupts many jailbreaks on an abliterated LLaMA while preserving most benign behavior.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CP tensor decomposition and layer-wise classifiers to identify jailbreak-related representations, then selectively bypasses layers at inference. It does not compute or intervene on the original harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction.
record.method_sensitivity: For the mitigation experiment, the susceptibility threshold is fixed at τ = 0.7; the authors describe it as tunable and as controlling the trade-off between mitigation and benign behavior preservation.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompt-mode CP factors from layer outputs and MHA outputs separate jailbreak from benign prompts with high F1 across 8 models, including Mamba, from early layers onward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak versus benign prompt type is linearly decodable from early-layer latent representations across architectures and alignment stages.

fits_no_version.finding: On the abliterated LLaMA-3.1-8B, susceptibility-guided layer bypass gives TP=78/100 and TN=94/100. MHA-only bypass gives TP=61 and TN=92. Disrupted outputs count as successful defenses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bypassing layers with high jailbreak-classifier probability disrupts many instruction-level jailbreaks while largely preserving benign outputs.

record.problems: The mitigation experiment is limited to one abliterated model and a held-out set of 200 prompts, with 100 prompts in each class. The authors state that the prompt sources primarily cover instruction-level attacks and exclude optimization-based attacks such as GCG and PAIR. No untreated baseline or uncertainty estimates are reported for the mitigation counts. The paper does not evaluate general capability beyond benign prompt behavior.
record.rows_left_out: The layer-by-layer F1 values in Figures 3 and 4 and the qualitative heatmaps in Figures 5 and 6 are not separately transcribed: the plotted layer values are not given as text, and these analyses concern prompt-type separability or localized representation changes rather than any listed refusal-direction version.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated or added. No refusal rate or capability check is reported.
Abliteration is assumed to remove safety. The abliterated model's refusal or compliance rate is never measured.
There is no test of whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction, and no adversarial training against ablation.
There is no comparison of single-direction, affine, cone or multi-direction accounts. The CP factors are jailbreak-classifier features, not refusal directions.
Harmfulness judgment and the refusal decision are not separated.
Classifier separability is compared across base, instruct and abliterated models. No refusal-direction transfer is tested.
Refusal training is not varied in relation to a removable direction.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from discusses/T6 to assumes/T4. The study relies on abliteration (V2) having removed safety, which it cites as a premise for choosing the testbed, and reports only its own method's performance. The original refusal-direction paper is not cited. 'Successful defense' includes incoherent or truncated outputs, so TP is not a refusal rate.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not find or intervene on a difference-in-means refusal direction, measure refusal induction, or test preservation of general capability.
No weight edit or abliteration based on the refusal direction is tested.
The study does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation increases robustness.
The study does not compare single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
It compares several model families and training stages for jailbreak-prompt classification, not transfer of a refusal direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
The study does not vary refusal training to test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.
No reasoning model is evaluated for the single-direction refusal claim.

rows.subject: all eight evaluated models (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Models include GPT-J-6B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, GPT-JT-6B, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct-Abliterated, and Mamba-2.8b-hf
rows.stage_stated: Base, instruction-tuned, abliterated, and state-space models
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate layer-wise jailbreak-versus-benign prompt classification using CP-decomposed hidden-state and attention representations.

conditions.value: Layer outputs and MHA outputs; Mamba mixer and block outputs
Jailbreak Classification dataset; sample count not stated

rows.measure: F1 score for classifying jailbreak versus benign prompts
rows.value: The paper reports consistently high F1 scores across all evaluated models; exact values are shown in figures.
rows.note: The text gives an aggregate verbal summary; layer-by-layer plotted values are not transcribed. This measures prompt-type separability, not refusal-direction mediation.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct-Abliterated
rows.operation_detail: Bypass layers selected by the latent-space susceptibility score, using threshold τ = 0.7.
rows.measure: Jailbreak defense outcomes / attack success rate
rows.note: The study counts disrupted or non-compliant outputs as successful defense. The intervention bypasses selected layers, not a refusal direction.
rows.check: This is the study's own defense method. The 22% ASR has no untreated baseline: the abliterated model's ASR without bypass is not reported. It therefore cannot show how much abliteration removed refusal (V2).

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct-Abliterated
rows.operation_detail: Bypass layers selected by the latent-space susceptibility score, using threshold τ = 0.7.
rows.note: The study treats disrupted outputs on benign prompts as false positives. This is not a general-capability evaluation.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct-Abliterated
rows.operation_detail: Bypass selected multi-head attention components based on susceptibility scores.
rows.measure: Jailbreak defense outcomes / attack success rate
rows.note: Comparator intervention; it bypasses attention components, not a refusal direction.
rows.check: Own-method comparator (MHA bypass) with no untreated baseline. It does not bear on any version.

rows.operation_detail: Bypass selected multi-head attention components based on susceptibility scores.
